name: Sour water stripping and amine regeneration
principle: Refinery sour water, which carries H2S and NH3 from hydroprocessing and coking, is flashed, then steam-stripped in a column. Stripped water returns to the refinery and the H2S and NH3 overhead goes to the sulfur recovery unit. Rich refinery amine from fuel gas and LPG treating is regenerated in a similar steam-stripping loop.

performance.metric: stripped sour water specifications and one- vs two-stage design
performance.unit: ppmw NH3 typical target (10-20 ppm when reused in crude desalter); NH3 column ~3.5 barg producing <5 ppmw H2S ammonia with scrubbing
performance.basis: Brimstone STS (Hatcher et al.): "Typical targets for NH3 are 30-80 ppmw" in stripped sour water; Lieberman (DigitalRefining/PTQ): when stripper bottoms are reused in the crude desalter "the NH3 content should be about 10 to 20 ppm"; BRE Sour Water paper: the ammonia column typically operates around 3.5 barg and with additional scrubbing can produce <5 ppmw H2S; two-stage sour water strippers are the most common technology (SDEWES journal; ResearchGate control-scheme study)

source.note: Brimstone STS Technical Paper 03V12, Hatcher et al., Sour Water Stripper Performance (read 2026-10-28); also digitalrefining.com/article/1000799 and bre.com Sour Water PDF
